segments: 120 Chronography of Bar Hebraeus.
Leo died,
and his son Constantine reigned thirty-four years.
And Artabasdos, his brother-in-law, rebelled against him,
and he entered Constantinople,
and sat in the palace.
The king, however, because he was outside,
fled from his Opsikion,
and took refuge with the Anatolics, and received an army from them,
and came to Amorium of Phrygia,
and wintered there.
Artabasdos, however, gathered an army and came against him,
and Artabasdos was defeated and fled.
And in the year 1056 [744 AD],
Hisham died at Rusafa of Callinicus.
After Hisham, Walid son of Yazid son of Abd [al-Malik reigned] one year and three months.
He harmed the members of Hisham's household,
and plundered their houses.
And he commanded, and the tongue of the Patriarch of the Chalcedonians in Syria was cut out.
And the Arabs hated him very much,
because he drank wine and strong drink,
and practiced the rest of evil deeds.
And on this account,
Fāsiq (Fāsiq,
Fāsiq?), that is, 'dissolute', they used to call (nickname) him.
Therefore Abbas son of Walid, the uncle of Walid son of Yazid, rose up against him,
and wanted to reign.
The Arabs, however, did not want him,
because he was the son of a concubine.
Rather, they made king {OCR?} his brother, Yazid son of Walid, in Damascus.
And he sent an army,
and they overtook Walid son of Yazid in the desert,
and cut off his head and fixed it upon a spear,
and hung with it a flagon of wine,
and brought it to Damascus.
[Af]ter {OCR?} Walid son of Yazid:
Yazid son of Walid, two months.
When, as we have said, this Yazid killed Walid his cousin,
a great division fell among the Arabs,
and in every region one rose up, not submitting to his fellow.
In the Jazira rose up Bastam;
and in Mosul, Said son of Hudhayl;
and in Wasit, Abdallah son of Umar the king [or: as king];
and in Armenia, Marwan;
and in Khorasan, the son of Sarig;
and in Africa, Abu Hudhayl.
As for Yazid, an ulcer broke out on him two months after he began to reign,
and he died.
After Yazid son of Walid, Ibrahim. This was a man of pleasant encounter,
and good by nature.
